Q122820005.summary: Christ sits at the top centre, haloed and raising both hands in blessing, as a dense crowd presses around him; below, figures bend over the gathered food and a large basket fills the foreground. The heavy, strongly modelled figures fill the panel so completely that little of the openwork ground remains. Part of the Magdeburg ivories made for Otto I's new archbishopric, the plaque celebrates Christ who feeds the multitude.
facts: The Louvre owns two of the sixteen surviving Magdeburg ivories; this one was given by a group of Friends of the Louvre in 1909.
Its history runs from Magdeburg Cathedral, probably via the Halle treasury, to the collections of Girolamo Possenti in Fabriano (sold 1880), Sigismond Bardac and Edouard Larcade.
Wikipedia's list of the plaques (after Fillitz) identifies the scene as the second miracle of the loaves and fishes, the feeding of the four thousand.
Q122820005.notes: Inv. OA 6310. The Louvre title does not specify which feeding is shown; the scripture follows the identification as the second (four thousand) feeding.
Q122820005.original_title: Plaque : Multiplication des pains et des poissons
